boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Mossy Creek record (December 29, 1863) in Operations about Dandridge [December 1863-January 1864]. The December 24 and 27 actions near Dandridge and Mossy Creek fall outside the frozen date and are not added. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen Confederate bound (2,000) is an imported figure and the Union bound is blank; this pass does not validate either as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen Confederate force text attributes to Sturgis a report of cavalry supported by a brigade of infantry, approximately 2,000 men; the live field reads zero. In the inspected passages Sturgis puts the enemy's entire cavalry at about 6,000 and, in a 3.15 p.m. dispatch, reports a division of infantry and two batteries with it. Martin says he engaged with all his guns and 2,000 men, that the force opposing him was at first not greater than 4,000 with two batteries, and that he later found three brigades of cavalry, six regiments of infantry and three batteries in his front.
claims.rationale: Each commander assigns the larger number to the other side; the inspected Sturgis passages do not contain the frozen text's brigade and 2,000 figure. None is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Martin says the ground from Talbott's Station to Mossy Creek was open, rolling tilled fields flanked by high woodland, and that he could not maneuver his artillery except near the railroad; he used a railroad cut on the flank of the advancing infantry. Sturgis says the enemy advanced over open ground where he was mowed down while the Union troops were largely sheltered.
claims.rationale: Ground described by interested accounts; no map verification. The field positions were chosen during the action and are not tagged inherited.

claims.value: Sturgis says he received information in the night of the 28th that a Confederate cavalry brigade had camped at Dandridge, sent much of his cavalry toward it, and recalled La Grange, and Foster and Wolford if they found no enemy, once he ascertained the enemy's strength; his dispatch says Wolford and Foster found no enemy at Dandridge because the whole Confederate force had moved to his front in the night. Martin says that on reconnoitering for another attack he found the Union force strongly posted and overlapping both his flanks, with a fresh brigade arriving.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from interested accounts; no message log inspected.

claims.value: Sturgis attributes much of the day's success to Brigadier General W. L. Elliott and describes Mott's infantry holding its fire, then charging with the bayonet. Martin commends Armstrong, Morgan and brigade commanders and says the retreat was made in perfect order. The frozen commanders are Major General William T. Martin and Brigadier General Samuel D. Sturgis; the live page gives Major General Samuel Sturgis and Colonel William Martin.
claims.rationale: Attributed judgments from interested accounts; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sturgis reported the enemy driven back about 4 miles in great confusion, with the pursuit not pushed beyond Talbott's Station because of darkness. Martin says his retreat was orderly and that at dusk the enemy was finally repulsed. NPS says the Confederates were back at their starting point by dark.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The characterizations of the Confederate withdrawal conflict.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total unknown (US 151; CS unknown); the live field reads 151 (US 151; CS 0). Sturgis's January 8 report gives 18 killed, 77 wounded and 5 missing, with a total read "LOO" in OCR (the components sum to 100, a computation here); his January 1 letter gives 96. He estimates Confederate losses at 250 to 400, says 44 prisoners were taken and 22 dead buried, while his evening dispatch says about 50 prisoners. Martin appends a casualty table not printed in the inspected OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Sturgis's own totals differ, and a compiled return (garbled in OCR) is not selected.

open_questions: Foster's telegram, Elliott's, McCook's, the brigade and battery reports, Mott's report, the compiled Union return and Armstrong's and Morgan's reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Sturgis's dispatches and reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXI Part 1 and XXXII Part 1, are one family of interested Union accounts; Martin's report, printed in Volume XXXI Part 1, is a separate family of interested Confederate accounts. The volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
